sharps.do1: Pick up only with tongs or thick gloves.
sharps.do2: Put in a hard, closed container (bottle or can).
sharps.dont1: Do not touch with bare hands.
sharps.dont2: Do not press, bend, or open it.
sharps.dont3: Do not throw in open waste.

glass.do1: Use thick gloves or a scoop to pick up.
glass.do2: Wrap broken pieces in cardboard or thick cloth.
glass.do3: Place in a sturdy bag clearly marked 'Glass'.
glass.dont2: Do not stomp or crush with feet.
glass.dont3: Do not mix with soft paper or food waste.

batteries.do2: Keep in a dry, ventilated box away from direct sun.
batteries.do3: Hand over to an authorised e-waste recycler.
batteries.dont1: Do not break, puncture, or burn batteries.
batteries.dont2: Do not mix leaking batteries with dry paper.
batteries.dont3: Do not throw into normal landfill bins.

chemicals.do1: Check label and keep container upright with lid tight.
chemicals.do2: Wear gloves and a face covering if fumes are strong.
chemicals.do3: Keep separate from other waste in a shady spot.
chemicals.dont1: Do not smell, pour, or taste unknown liquids.
chemicals.dont2: Do not mix different chemicals together.
chemicals.dont3: Do not empty contents down open drains or soil.

medical.do1: Use thick gloves and a face mask.
medical.do2: Isolate in a yellow or red sealed bag if available.
medical.do3: Inform hospital staff or municipal bio-waste handler.
medical.dont1: Do not handle open bandages, tubes, or syringes.
medical.dont2: Do not mix bio-waste with household scrap.
medical.dont3: Do not attempt to wash or reuse single-use items.

general.do1: Sort cleanly into dry plastic, paper, or metal piles.
general.do2: Rinse food residue to prevent foul smells.
general.do3: Flatten cardboard and crush clean plastic bottles.
general.dont1: Do not mix dirty wet waste with dry recyclables.
general.dont2: Do not burn plastic or rubber scrap.
general.dont3: Do not leave scattered in rainy weather.

unknown.do1: Stop. Do not touch or move this item.
unknown.do2: Warn coworkers and people nearby to keep distance.
unknown.do3: Report the hazard to municipal staff or supervisor.
unknown.dont1: Do not pick up with bare hands or feet.
unknown.dont2: Do not break, crush, or open mystery packages.
unknown.dont3: Do not put in your collection sack.

sharps.title: Safe Handling of Sharps
sharps.step1: Never use bare hands to pick up syringes, razor blades, or broken needles. Always inspect the waste pile before grabbing.
sharps.step2: Use metal tongs or puncture-resistant thick leather gloves to handle sharp objects safely.
sharps.step3: Place sharps inside a puncture-proof container, like an empty thick plastic bottle or tin can with a lid.
sharps.step4: Seal the container, label it clearly if possible, and alert your supervisor or collection lead.
sharps.q1: What should you wear when picking up a used syringe?
sharps.q1_opt1: Thick puncture-resistant gloves or use tongs
sharps.q2: Where should used needles be deposited?
sharps.q2_opt0: In a hard, puncture-proof closed container
sharps.q3: What must you do if you accidentally get poked by a needle?
sharps.q3_opt1: Bandage it and wait a week
sharps.q3_opt2: Wash with soap and water immediately and seek doctor care

glass.title: Broken Glass & Sharp Metal
glass.step1: Look carefully for glass shards before reaching into bags or heaps. Broken glass causes the most hand lacerations.
glass.step2: Pick up large shards using heavy-duty gloves. Never kick or crush glass with your boots.
glass.step3: Wrap broken glass in folded cardboard or thick sacking before placing it into transport bins.
glass.step4: Keep glass containers separate from bags with paper and plastics so coworkers are not cut during loading.
glass.q1: Why should you never crush glass with your footwear?
glass.q1_opt0: Glass shards can pierce soles and injure your feet
glass.q1_opt1: It ruins the recyclability of glass
glass.q1_opt2: It creates dust that blows away
glass.q2: What is the best way to package broken glass?
glass.q2_opt0: Tossed loose into a cloth sack
glass.q2_opt2: Wrapped in cardboard or stiff carton
glass.q3: Which tool helps collect small scattered glass pieces?

batteries.title: Batteries & E-Waste Handling
batteries.step1: Lithium-ion phone and laptop batteries can ignite or explode if punctured or crushed.
batteries.step2: Never drop batteries into general wet or combustible waste. Store them in a dry, shaded container.
batteries.step3: If a battery looks swollen, discolored, or leaking liquid, do not press it. Cover terminals with tape if possible.
batteries.step4: Sell or hand over batteries to authorized e-waste buyers who pay fair rates and recycle safely.
batteries.q1: What is the danger of crushing a lithium-ion battery?
batteries.q1_opt1: It can spark and cause a chemical fire
batteries.q2: How should batteries be stored while sorting?
batteries.q2_opt0: In a dry, ventilated box away from heat and water
batteries.q3: What should you do with a swollen phone battery?
batteries.q3_opt1: Pierce it to let gas out
batteries.q3_opt2: Handle gently without pressure and keep in fire-safe sand or container

chemicals.title: Hazardous Chemical Containers
chemicals.step1: Bottles of pesticide, toilet cleaners, and industrial solvents contain toxic residues and corrosive acids.
chemicals.step2: Never smell, inhale, or pour mystery liquid out of unlabeled cans. Vapors can cause lung damage.
chemicals.step3: Keep caps screwed on tightly. Store containers upright to prevent spillage onto your clothing or feet.
chemicals.step4: Keep chemical cans separated from paper, cardboard, and other combustible scrap materials.
chemicals.q1: What should you do if an unlabelled bottle has strong fumes?
chemicals.q1_opt0: Sniff it closely to identify the chemical
chemicals.q1_opt2: Step back, do not inhale, and keep it upright in safe isolation
chemicals.q2: Can empty pesticide containers be reused for drinking water?
chemicals.q2_opt0: Never; toxic residues remain and cause poisoning
chemicals.q2_opt1: Yes, if washed with hot water once
chemicals.q2_opt2: Yes, after leaving in the sun
chemicals.q3: Why must you keep chemical bottles upright?
chemicals.q3_opt0: To make them easier to count
chemicals.q3_opt1: To prevent leaks onto skin, shoes, or flammable materials

medical.title: Medical & Bio-Waste Awareness
medical.step1: Used bandages, blood tubing, cotton swabs, and surgical gloves carry contagious pathogens and viral infections.
medical.step2: Recognize biohazard markings: yellow bags, red bins, and bio-hazard trefoil symbols.
medical.step3: Never attempt to wash and resell single-use medical items like masks, catheters, or dialysis tubes.
medical.step4: Report illegal dumping of hospital waste to municipal authorities or community supervisors immediately.
medical.q1: What color bags are typically used for clinical infectious waste?
medical.q2: Why should single-use medical masks and gloves never be reused?
medical.q2_opt0: They carry bacteria, viruses, and biological fluids
medical.q2_opt1: They weigh too little for scrap value
medical.q2_opt2: They take too long to dry
medical.q3: What should you do if hospital waste is dumped in public garbage bins?
medical.q3_opt0: Sort through it with bare hands
medical.q3_opt2: Report the hazard to municipal sanitary inspectors
